On Wed, Mar 3, 2027 at 11:28 AM Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com> wrote:

Naomi —

High-level thinking: BrightLayer looks like a strong fit for a tiered reserved offer. My recommended structure:

1) GPU pool sizing (two SKU approach):
   - Reranker pool: 6x A100-80GB nodes (target steady throughput; reserve for batch spikes)
   - Chat pool: 8x A100-40GB nodes (reduce cost per token for interactive workloads)
   - Optional small burst pool (3x A10) enabled for 10% of peak minute bursts

2) Throughput guarantees / SLOs:
   - Baseline availability SLA: 99.5% (monthly) for reserved pools; p95 latency targets: chat < 120ms, rerank p95 for 128-token sequences < 300ms.
   - Penalty ladder: service credits only if both latency and availability breach (protects from noisy-burst edge cases).

3) Reserved commit pricing / discount bands (ballpark):
   - 12-month commit: ~28% off list hosted-equivalent unit price (applies to reserved capacity utilization up to committed units)
   - 24-month commit: ~38% off list (volume tiers apply: higher commits get stepped discounts)

4) Conversion credits and bridge months (proposal):
   - Offer conversion credits equal to 50% of their average hosted spend for month 0, 30% for month 1, 15% for month 2.
   - Bridge months: allow hosted overage free-burst into dedicated pools for up to 2 bridge months (capped by agreed burst pool size).
   - Require minimum 6-month billing commit (to avoid month-to-month churn).

5) Guardrails:
   - Burst caps and overage rates after bridge months (clear unit economics).
   - Minimum committed baseline must be >= 50% of 3-month average hosted usage.

If you want to be more promotional for a fast close, we can bump month0 credit to 60% or add one free month of premium support. But that increases churn risk.

Happy to refine numbers.
